allocator_state_note: A pre-timing reference scan can leave allocator cache reserved. Absolute peak allocated is stable across repeats; the first repeat peak reserved may include that retained cache, while repeats 2-3 show the method-specific reserved peak. Both absolute peaks and increments over the recorded input baseline are reported; no retry was performed.
conclusion: All three chunk sizes preserved outputs, carried state and all six input gradients within the preregistered FP32 thresholds at both lengths. In this isolated component measurement, chunk64 had the lowest median synchronized forward+backward time at both lengths; the ordering was chunk64 < chunk32 < chunk16 < scan. This is component-only evidence, not a full-model or production-kernel speed claim.
limitations: Two lengths, one seed and three synchronized repeats; descriptive component timing only.
The scan reference is a Python recurrence; the chunk path is multiple triangular solves. Differences include launch/Python overhead and are not kernel-level attribution.
Peak memory is allocator data; first-repeat reserved memory can include retained cache from the pre-timing reference scan.
The existing delta_chunk is a small finite-log-decay oracle, not a production kernel.
No full-model, sustained-throughput, quality, training or architecture-superiority claim.
next_question: Integrate the numerically qualified chunk composition behind an opt-in GDN algorithm flag in a separate reviewed IMP and compare full Nano forward/backward at T512/T2048 against scan with exact full-model loss/gradient gates and full-model memory/timing; no production kernel claim from this component result.

oracle_limitations: delta_chunk is an independent dense triangular solve intended as a small finite-log-decay oracle, not a production kernel.
It has no built-in chunking; T0024 composes it over caller-selected consecutive slices with carried FP32 state.
Existing GDN numerical tests are small float64/NumPy cases; they do not cover FP32 projected-tensor gradients at T512/T2048 or CUDA resource behavior.
The full-slice chunk solve is O(T^2) in the slice length; composition changes the cost profile but is not a custom kernel.
This is a component feasibility test only; it does not show that GDN dominates the full model or that a production kernel is faster.
